record.cosmo_tool: Calibration against a fixed standard sky plus each exposure's own noise model, instead of comparison stars taken the same night.
record.credit: The healthy reference is the IAM Sequencing Atlas, built on the sorted-cell methylation atlas of Loyfer N., Magenheim J., Peretz A. et al. (2023) A DNA methylation atlas of normal human cell types, Nature 613:355-364, acknowledged as prior work. Uncertainty combined by JCGM 100:2008 (GUM). Correcting each sample from its own reads, without same-batch healthy controls, is IAM's method.
record.field_how: Atlas-referenced readings compare the sample with the healthy cell-type reference (the IAM Sequencing Atlas), measured once. Laboratory and library effects are corrected from the sample's own reads: its false-methylation rate at CpG islands that no healthy cell methylates, the library's noise floor at the sites read, the expectation at its own read depth, and its own cell composition. No same-batch healthy controls are needed. IAM-A uses no outside reference at all.

questions: Why no healthy samples from the same run?
They cannot be certified healthy and are rarely available; the atlas is checkable by anyone, and each sample's own reads give its laboratory part.
What is each sample's methylation reading actually compared against to judge whether it looks healthy?

Readings are compared with the IAM Sequencing Atlas (recorded as IAM-Atlas v2.1 and the IAM Sequencing Atlas), not with healthy samples run alongside the sample. One instrument, IAM-A, uses no outside reference at all.
field_how; outputs[0] 'Healthy references used'
If you're not using same-run healthy controls, how do you correct for differences between labs or sequencing runs?

Lab and library effects are worked out from the sample's own reads: its false-methylation rate at CpG islands no healthy cell methylates, the library's noise floor at the sites read, what's expected at its own read depth, and its own cell-type mixture.
field_how; rules[0].rule
Why not just include healthy samples processed in the same run as controls, as is conventional?

Same-run samples can't be certified as truly healthy and are often unavailable. The atlas, by contrast, can be checked by any researcher, and each sample's own reads supply the lab-specific correction instead.
existing_qa; rules[0].why
How do you guarantee the reference files used in a run are the genuine, unaltered ones?
Before a run starts, every runtime file is checked against its SHA-256 fingerprint listed in a reference manifest file. If a file is missing from that list or has been changed, the run is stopped.
rules[0].rule
Has this file-fingerprint check ever actually caught or refused a bad file in practice?

Yes, once, by accident on 2026-11-22: a summary file was placed in the atlas reference folder without a manifest entry, and the check stopped every run (50 libraries) before any reading began, until the file was moved out. No reading was made against an unlisted file.
instrument history 2026-11-22; reference door record
Is the older method, using same-run healthy samples as a tare, still sitting in the codebase?

No. On a sequenced sample the same-run tare options are refused, and the word 'untared' no longer appears in any reading or note: every atlas-referenced reading states the IAM Sequencing Atlas as its reference. The option stays only for arrays.
chain update of 2026-11-22 (reference block on sequencing)
Has the laboratory correction been tested with a planted known answer?

Yes. Incomplete bisulfite conversion was planted in the known-answer library (1% of unmethylated calls turned methylated). The laboratory part, read at the always-unmarked islands, rose by 0.00973 against 0.0099 predicted, while IAM-A, the held error and the Law Sphere hold moved by less than 0.3%.
